note: The Burmese drum-circle orchestra heard at theatre, festivals and spirit rites: a ring of tuned drums, gong circles and a piercing oboe that jump between tempos without warning. Titles are romanised differently on every release; dates are release years (the UNESCO orchestra was recorded in 1977).

size.basis: No source counts recordings. Discogs returns 36 hits for 'hsaing waing', of which about ten are releases of the ensemble itself: Folkways' 1950s Burmese survey, Ocora's 1981 'Birmanie: Musique d'art', the UNESCO/Auvidis disc (recorded 1977, issued 2001), Seven Seas' 1992 Tokyo session (reissued 2008), Kyaw Kyaw Naing's 1998 Shanachie album, Sublime Frequencies' nat pwe cassettes and a few untitled Burmese tapes. Behind them is a large, uncatalogued domestic cassette, VCD and radio output for zat pwe, anyeint, puppet and nat ensembles, the five types Burmese scholarship recognises, each with its own repertoire of tunes; the range is a judgement. Core: the theatre overtures, dance suites and best-known pieces a hsaing player would expect to know.
